ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The curve on the left shows the action potential of a myocardial fiber; the membrane potential first rapidly rises to near a positive value, then maintains a relatively long plateau phase between about 0.1 and 0.3 seconds, and finally repolarizes and decreases again. The permeability curve on the right shows a brief early spike in Na+ permeability, while Ca2+ permeability remains elevated for a relatively long time, corresponding to the plateau phase. Reasoning: The question asks about a major difference between the action potential of a myocardial fiber and that of a skeletal muscle fiber. The long plateau in the figure indicates that the duration of depolarization of the myocardial action potential is longer; in contrast, the skeletal muscle action potential is usually very short and has no obvious long plateau phase. Therefore, the major difference is that the duration of depolarization/action potential of the myocardial fiber is prolonged.
